result.keywords: This article examines informal audio environments in evening street markets, with attention to portable loudspeakers, vendor call patterns, ambient music layering, and pedestrian movement. Through ethnographic observation and short-form interviews, the study maps how sound contributes to place identity, navigation, and social negotiation in dense commercial corridors. The analysis distinguishes between fixed installation sounds and transient human-made cues, and proposes a descriptive framework for comparing market soundscapes across districts.
result.title: Whispering Tides in Ceramic Glass: A Curatorial Survey of Night Market Soundscapes.
